Using rotation: let $\theta=\mathrm{A\hat{K}N}=\mathrm{L\hat{K}N}$

Move the diagram $1$ unit to the right. Then $\mathrm{A}'$ is $\mathrm{L}'$ rotated through $2\theta$.

$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\mathrm{AN}}{\mathrm{KA}}=\dfrac{2}{4}=\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\sin 2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta=2\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)=\dfrac{4}{5}$

$\cos 2\theta=\cos^{2}\theta-\sin^{2}\theta=\dfrac{3}{5}$

$x_{\mathrm{A}'}=x_{\mathrm{L}'}\cos 2\theta-y_{\mathrm{L}'}\sin 2\theta=4\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)=\dfrac{12}{5}$

$y_{\mathrm{A}'}=x_{\mathrm{L}'}\sin 2\theta+y_{\mathrm{L}'}\cos 2\theta=4\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)=\dfrac{16}{5}$

$\mathrm{A}'\left(\dfrac{12}{5};\dfrac{16}{5}\right)$

Now to get back to $\mathrm{A}$, move back $1$ unit to the left.

$\therefore\mathrm{A}\left(\dfrac{7}{5};\dfrac{16}{5}\right)$

parts.working_md:
$\mathrm{LHS}=\dfrac{1-\cos 2x-\sin x}{\sin 2x-\cos x}$

$=\dfrac{1-(1-2\sin^{2}x)-\sin x}{2\sin x\cos x-\cos x}$

$=\dfrac{2\sin^{2}x-\sin x}{2\sin x\cos x-\cos x}$

$=\dfrac{\sin x(2\sin x-1)}{\cos x(2\sin x-1)}$

$=\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\tan x=\mathrm{RHS}$

steps.description: either $\sin x(2\sin x-1)$ or $\cos x(2\sin x-1)$

parts.working_md:
The minute hand moves through $360^{\circ}$ in $60$ minutes.

The hour hand moves through $30^{\circ}$ in $60$ minutes, that is, $\dfrac{1}{12}$ that of the minute hand.

So when the minute hand moves through $222^{\circ}$, the hour hand moves through $\dfrac{222^{\circ}}{12}=18{,}5^{\circ}$.

alternatives.label: OR

$\therefore$ it moves through $\dfrac{37}{60}\times 30^{\circ}=18{,}5^{\circ}$ in $37$ minutes
